asy.scope.mixedWarn: {n} domains are present and the scope is set to All. A single statistic across mixed populations can be wrong in both directions at once — narrow the scope above to compute this per domain.
asy.tc.noDataInScope: {elem} has no positive values in the current domain scope. Pick a different element from the selector, or widen the scope above.

asy.dm.bndHardAdvice: Grades differ sharply across the contact — the split is doing real work. Keep the domains separate and do not let grade cross the boundary during estimation.
asy.dm.bndSoftAdvice: Grades are alike across the contact — the split may not be doing much. Consider whether these domains need to be separate, or treat the boundary as soft during estimation.
asy.dm.bndTransitionalAdvice: Between hard and soft. Look at the contact profile and the geology before deciding how to treat this boundary.
asy.dm.bndFarApartAdvice: The nearest samples in other domains sit many drill spacings away, so these domains do not actually meet anywhere the drilling can see. There is no contact here to measure — treat the discontinuity figure above as meaningless rather than as a hard or soft verdict.
asy.fromCore: Bring data over from Orebit Core:
qi.fit.poor: Not a good fit — try a different distribution
asy.tc.recordHint: Every cap currently in force, with the parameters that produced it — this is what a resource report has to justify. Capping is always recomputed from the original data, so changing a threshold or undoing it is safe.
qi.topcut.statsArePostCap: — statistics below are post-cap; change or undo it in the Top-Cut tab
asy.pcaArrowLength: Arrow length ∝ the variable's contribution to the PC. The angle between arrows
asy.logXformHelp: Creates a new column {col} = ln(grade) without touching the original. This is a diagnostic and export aid — it is not consumed by the Resource estimation stage, and there is no back-transform in the app. Use it to inspect a skewed distribution, to read correlations on log values, or to hand log grades to other software. Most useful when the QQ R² is high (close to log-normal).
asy.overlayNote: Element distributions are normalized (P99 = 1.0) so they overlay on the same axis. Useful for comparing distribution shape.
asy.bdlNote: sit exactly at the smallest positive value {value} {unit} — most likely a sentinel standing in for below-detection-limit (DL/2). Statistics below are computed on the substituted values; mean and median may be biased low. For audit reproducibility, report using the BDL samples column below.
asy.topcutTableNote: ▼ green = value decreased. Capping is always recomputed from the original data, so you can change the threshold freely. Justifying a top-cut →
asy.lithoVerdictStrong: Means differ significantly — domaining by lithology is advised
asy.lithoVerdictModerate: Means differ moderately — consider domaining by lithology
asy.lithoVerdictWeak: Means are similar — lithology is not the primary domain
asy.nnSourceNote: Source: collar position (top-of-hole, smallest from_m per hole). For an inclined hole the collar is the valid surface location.
asy.domainVerdictSparse: very sparse — green-field exploration, small mineralized zone
asy.domainVerdictLimited: mineralization is limited — focus on the high/medium-grade subset
asy.domainVerdictBalanced: balanced distribution — domaining by lithology is effective

asy.dc.declusterHint: Weights each sample by 1/(samples in its grid cell) to correct clustered-drilling bias. Grid default = 1.5× median drill spacing between holes ({g}m) — not sample spacing, which is downhole and much smaller. Learn more →
asy.dm.boundaryHow: For each sample, its grade is compared with the mean grade of the 5 nearest samples in other domains. High discontinuity means grades differ strongly across the contact — a hard boundary. Low discontinuity means they are alike — a soft, gradational boundary. Neither is good or bad; they call for different treatment during estimation.
asy.dm.discHint: High discontinuity = hard boundary (keep domains apart). Low discontinuity = soft boundary (the split may not be doing much). Complements ANOVA, which tests mean differences but not spatial behaviour at the contact.
asy.dm.ruleD2: P33 ≤ grade < P80 in host litho
asy.tc.reviewP99Only: Review P99 only if geological outliers justify it
asy.kcmiFillHint: Section 1 commentary is auto-generated from the dataset. The reporting standards table below must be filled in with project-specific knowledge.
asy.biplotDegenerate: Arrow labels are hidden for {vars}: their loading vectors are effectively zero-length (no variance in this dataset), so the labels would stack on the origin. The variables are still included in the PCA.

asy.st.gradeContribHint: Samples sorted highest-grade first, against cumulative % of total metal — a steeper curve means fewer samples carry the deposit. How to read this →
asy.st.qqHint: Points close to the diagonal indicate a log-normal distribution — a candidate for a log-transform before kriging.
asy.st.compareHint: Click a card to select the active element. CV: <1.5 normal · 1.5–3 high · >3 critical. What CV means for top-cut →

asy.dm.cutoffHint: Mineralised = grade at or above the cut-off. Choose it from the break in the log-probability plot (Stats tab), not from a percentile; the starting value is P80.
asy.dm.geoValidBody: Statistical domains are data-driven, not geological — always check boundaries against logged lithology and your interpretation. Why this matters for JORC →
asy.dm.renameHint: Rename domains into geological labels ("Main Lode", "Oxide Cap") — the names carry through into the plots, the master CSV, and the JORC/KCMI commentary.

asy.mv.biplotLegend: Points = samples, coloured by lithology; red arrows = element loading vectors, length and angle both meaningful. How to read a biplot →
asy.mv.standardizedHint: Every variable is converted to a z-score first, so units alone don't decide the result. Why PCA is standardised →
asy.mv.droppedConst: Excluded from this PCA because their values never vary: {cols}.
asy.mv.ambiguousAxes: The first two components explain almost the same amount of variance, so the PC1/PC2 directions are not well determined. Read the grouping, not the exact axis orientation.
asy.bv.methodHint: Spearman is the default because assay grades are strongly skewed. Pearson vs Spearman, and when they disagree →
asy.bv.disagreeHint: Pairs whose Pearson and Spearman values differ by {thr} or more — the gap itself is the finding. Why they disagree →
asy.bv.disagreeNone: No pair differs materially between Pearson and Spearman. On this dataset the linear correlation is not being driven by outliers.
asy.bv.readingMissed: Pearson understates it — a real association that the linear measure nearly misses
asy.bv.readingSpurious: Pearson overstates it — the association largely disappears once ranks are used
asy.bv.zeroHeavy: Mostly zeros, so treat any correlation involving these with care: {cols} (not removed — that call is the geologist's). Why a zero-heavy column biases correlation →
asy.dm.cpTitle: Contact Profile — grade across the domain boundary
asy.dm.cpHint: Mean grade plotted against distance either side of the contact. A step at the contact means a hard boundary; a curve that flattens out means a soft, gradational one. Distance to the contact is approximated by the distance to the nearest sample of the other domain — with point data and no wireframe that is a proxy, not an exact distance to a surface.
asy.dm.cpAxisDist: Signed distance to contact (m) — negative = first domain, positive = second
asy.dm.cpVerdictHard: Hard boundary — the grade contrast survives right up to the contact, so grade should not be allowed to cross it during estimation.
asy.dm.cpVerdictSoft: Soft boundary — the contrast collapses near the contact, so the grades mix across it. Consider a soft boundary in estimation, or whether the split is needed at all.
asy.dm.cpVerdictTransitional: Transitional — the contrast weakens near the contact but does not disappear. Look at the profile shape and the geology before deciding.
asy.dm.cpVerdictNodiff: The two domains have practically the same grade everywhere, contact or not, so there is no discontinuity to classify. That is a different finding from a soft boundary.
asy.dm.cpVerdictUnknown: Not enough grade contrast between these domains to classify the contact.
asy.dm.cpRatio: contrast at contact {near} vs far field {far} — ratio {ratio}
asy.dm.cpTransitionWidth: Grades reach their own domain background about {w} m from the contact — treat that as the width of the transition zone.
asy.dm.cpScaleNote: Scale matters: a contact can look hard at sample spacing and soft at the block size an estimate is actually run on. Change the bin width to see the contact at the scale you will estimate on.
asy.dm.cpNoContact: No domain pair has enough samples on both sides to build a contact profile.
asy.dm.cpNoProfile: Not enough samples per distance bin for this pair. Try a wider bin, or a pair with more data on both sides.
asy.tc.diagTitle: Top-cut diagnostics — reading the tail, not just a percentile
asy.tc.diagHint: A percentile alone says nothing about why that percentile — these three plots are meant to be read together. How to read these three together →
asy.tc.diagNotApproved: Nothing here is applied automatically. These are the grounds for a decision that remains the geologist's, and whichever cut is chosen still has to be entered and applied above.
asy.tc.logProbHint: A single log-normal population plots as a straight line. Where the points bend away from the fitted body, the upper tail has stopped belonging to that population.
asy.tc.meanVarHint: How the capped mean and the coefficient of variation respond as the cut comes down. A cut that barely moves the mean but drops CV sharply is doing useful work.
asy.tc.cumMetalHint: The share of contained metal, and the share of samples, sitting above each cut. A few samples carrying a large share of the metal is the case top-cutting exists for.
asy.tc.disintCompare: Capping there would remove {loss}% of contained metal. For comparison, P98 = {p98} and P99 = {p99}.
asy.tc.disintNone: No disintegration detected — the upper tail does not depart from the body of the distribution, so there is no statistical case for a top-cut on this element. Capping anyway would remove metal without a reason to point at.
asy.tc.tooFewForCurves: Only {n} positive values — below {min} these curves are too unstable to read, so they are not shown rather than shown misleadingly.
asy.tc.exclHint: Exclusion removes a sample from the estimate altogether — the stronger claim, which is why a written reason is required. Capping vs. exclusion →
asy.tc.exclReasonPlaceholder: e.g. re-assay confirmed contamination in these intervals
asy.tc.exclReasonRequired: A reason is required. An exclusion that cannot be justified in writing should not be made.
asy.tc.exclNoneAbove: No samples sit above that threshold, so nothing would be excluded.
asy.tc.exclAlready: This element already has an exclusion. Undo it first to change the threshold.
asy.tc.exclTooMany: {pct}% of samples removed — past a few percent this is data selection, not outlier handling. Be ready to defend it.
asy.tc.exclActive: {n} of {total} samples excluded above {thr} {u}, removing {metal}% of contained metal.
asy.tc.exclFlagNote: Marked in the export as {col} so the removal is visible downstream instead of looking like missing data.
asy.tc.exclIndicator: As an indicator: {pct}% of samples sit above {thr} {u} and carry {metal}% of the contained metal. When a domain is the better answer →
asy.st.nscoreHelp: Creates {col}, the Gaussian equivalent of each grade, and stores the value-to-score table needed to come back. This is the transform sequential Gaussian simulation expects and the correct route for strongly skewed data — unlike the log transform, it is reversible. It is not consumed by the Resource stage, and that is not an oversight: Resource estimates by IDW, ordinary kriging and nearest neighbour, all of which work on the grades themselves. Normal scores are for simulation, so this column exists to be exported to software that runs it, with the back-transform available here for checking round trips.
asy.st.nscoreTooFew: Too few values to build a normal-score transform (at least 10 needed).
asy.st.nscoreTies: {tied} value(s) share a grade with another sample and were given the same score. Averaging ties avoids inventing an ordering the data does not contain, at the cost of the scores not being perfectly Gaussian where ties are heavy — common with repeated below-detection values.
asy.st.nscoreTailRule: Back-transforming a score beyond the observed range returns the observed extreme rather than extrapolating, because no measurement supports a grade outside what was actually seen.
asy.bv.mkRatioHint: A correlation you can act on. This writes a real column in the dataset, which leaves with the raw interval export (Domain tab) for use in other software. Nothing in Assay itself plots it spatially yet. Why ratios, and how this works →
asy.bv.ratioZeroRule: Rows whose denominator is zero or missing are left blank rather than given a value. Writing Infinity would poison every downstream statistic and read as a real number in an export.
asy.bv.ratioBadCols: Could not find both columns for that ratio.
asy.bv.ratioSameCol: Numerator and denominator are the same column — that ratio is 1 everywhere.
asy.mv.actionsTitle: Carry this into the rest of the workflow
asy.mv.actionsHint: The biplot shows structure; these turn it into columns other tabs can use.
asy.mv.savePcHint: Writes pc1_score and pc2_score as real columns for every complete case. They leave with the raw interval export (Domain tab) for use in other software; Assay itself does not yet plot them spatially. How this works →
asy.mv.pcNotReady: Run the PCA first — no scores available yet.
asy.mv.clusterHint: Clusters the standardised variables and writes cluster_kmeans. Seeding is deterministic, so the same data gives the same grouping every run — a grouping that changed between runs could not go in a report.
asy.mv.clusterNotDomain: These are statistical clusters, not geological domains. Nothing is written to the domain column: review them against the geology and set domains yourself in the Domain tab.
asy.mv.clusterTooFew: Too few complete cases for that many groups.
asy.mv.boxSkipped: Not shown, fewer than {min} samples — a box built from one or two values invents a distribution that is not there: {groups}
asy.sp.classQaqcUnknown: This classification rests on drill spacing alone. No QC samples were found, so the quality of the assays behind it is unverified — a Measured claim needs data confidence, not just close drilling.
asy.sp.classQaqcFail: QAQC has failing standards or contaminated blanks. Until that is resolved, the spacing-based classes above overstate the confidence the data supports.
asy.sp.classQaqcOk: QAQC checks pass, so the spacing-based classes above are not contradicted by data quality.
asy.dash.pendingTopcut: High-variability element(s) with no top-cut or exclusion reviewed yet
asy.dash.pendingQaqcNone: No QC samples detected — assay quality is unverified
asy.dash.pendingQaqcCert: Standards detected but certified values not entered, so they cannot be judged
asy.dash.pendingDomain: No domains defined yet — everything is being treated as one population
asy.derivedExportNote: Derived columns travel with the domain-tagged raw interval export (Domain tab). They are deliberately absent from the composited Master CSV, because length-weighting them is not meaningful: the average of Pb/Zn is not the ratio of the averages, and the average of normal scores is not the normal score of the average. Composite the raw grades, then derive again if you need these at composite support.
asy.hist.title: What has been done to this data
asy.hist.hint: {total} treatment(s) recorded, {changes} of which changed the grade values. This is the full audit trail — it also appears in the Report tab.
asy.hist.none: Nothing has been applied yet. The data is exactly as it was loaded.
asy.hist.beforeAfter: before: n={n0}, mean {m0}, CV {c0} → after: n={n1}, mean {m1}, CV {c1}
asy.hist.addedNoChange: A new column was added. The original grades were not touched, which is why the statistics do not move.
asy.hist.exclSummary: Excluded {n} sample(s) above {thr}, removing {metal}% of contained metal — reason: {reason}
asy.hist.pcSummary: Added pc1_score and pc2_score for {n} samples
asy.pipelineStatsActive: {list} — new columns created, original grades unchanged. Click to see the record on the Dashboard.
asy.pipelineRatioActive: Ratio column(s) created: {list}. Click to see the record on the Dashboard.
asy.pipelineMvActive: PC scores or clusters saved as columns. Click to see the record on the Dashboard.
asy.bv.mkRatioShort: Turn a correlation into a column you can map and export.
asy.mv.actionsShort: Turn the structure above into columns the other tabs can use.
asy.dm.cpShort: Grade either side of the contact — a step means hard, a curve means soft.
asy.dm.discShort: How sharply grade changes across each domain contact.
asy.hist.orderNote: Order matters for changes: each one is computed on what the previous step produced. Undoing any step rebuilds the column from the raw data and re-applies the rest.
asy.hist.noEffectNow: This step currently removes nothing — the steps before it already brought every value below its threshold. It stays in the list because changing an earlier step can make it bite again.
asy.hist.unknown: This project was saved before the treatment record existed, so what was applied to it is not known. The grades may already be capped or have samples excluded — check the Top-Cut tab and compare against the original CSV before relying on them.
asy.indicator.label: Data history ({n})
asy.indicator.changed: {n} treatment(s) changed the grade values. Click to review the full record and undo if needed.
asy.indicator.addedOnly: Columns were added; the original grades are unchanged. Click to review the record.
asy.cmp.previewNature: This is a scenario, not an edit — changing a parameter here never touches your raw interval data, only what you export. How compositing and treatments stay non-destructive →
asy.rp.csvHint: The three exports most people want, gathered here because this is where you come to export. Each also sits on the tab that produces it.
asy.rp.csvMaster: Master CSV — composites for the estimation stage
asy.rp.csvRaw: Raw intervals CSV — with domains and derived columns
asy.rp.csvElsewhere: Other exports live on their own tabs — Litho, Top-Cut, Domain — plus the compliance checklist below. Every tab, what it does →
asy.dm.rangeClipped: View zoomed to the main cluster; {n} hole(s) sit far enough outside it to compress everything else into a corner if shown at full scale.
import.title.warn: Import complete — check the notes below
import.title.blocked: Import not applied — required columns are missing
import.rejected: {n} row(s) rejected by the parser and NOT loaded:
import.missing: Required columns not identified: {roles}. Map them below.
import.warn.no_grade_columns: No grade column was recognised. The file loads, but nothing can be estimated from it until one is mapped.
import.gradeCodes: {bdl} below-detection value(s) (negative = detection limit) set to half the limit; {missing} missing-sample code(s) (e.g. -99, -999, -9999) set to blank and excluded.
import.warn.no_grade_columns_required: No grade column was recognised. This module cannot work without one — choose the commodity column below.
asy.export3d.needXyzSolids: Spatial coordinates (midx/midy/midz) are required for 3D solids
asy.export3d.noSolids: No 3D solids could be built — domains are coplanar or have fewer than 4 samples with XYZ
asy.unitAssumedPct: Unit not declared, assumed % (all values are 100 or below):
asy.unitAssumedPctHint: If these columns are actually ppm, set the unit in the grade column setting before compositing.
asy.tc.bodyDeparture: The distribution departs from a single lognormal population already at {v} {u} (P{p}), inside its body rather than in a sparse upper tail. That is a mixture or a differently shaped distribution, not a top-cut signal: capping there would remove real metal. Separate the populations with a domain, then look at each domain's upper tail.
